A B S T R A C T
In this work, we develop a novel safranine (SA)-based acidic sulfate copper electronic plating process for
through-hole copper void-free filling for high-quality electronics interconnection, and both the molecule actions
and synergistic effects of safranine (SA) are carefully explored. Cyclic voltammetry experiments at rotating rates
of 200 r/min and 1200 r/min demonstrate that SA itself can accelerate the electro-reduction of copper ion,
heighten the inhibiting effect of polyethylene glycol (PEG) and acceleration effect of bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide
(SPS). The addition of SA to the virgin make-up solution (VMS) containing PEG and SPS makes the relative
electric charge (ΔQ) between the low and high rotating rates be increased from 1.27 ± 0.04–22.53% ± 0.05,
indicating the higher copper electronic plating amount at the center than that at the mouth of through-hole. In
situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy together with theoretical calculations further illustrate that the
molecule SA is adsorbed on the copper surface through the N atom in the aromatic ring, PEG and SPS can
heighten the adsorption of SA on the Cu surface, and both PEG and SPS both synergistically influence with SA to
achieve the void-free copper filling of through-hole.

1. Introduction
With the rapid development of electronic products, advanced fabri-
cation technologies for high-density interconnect (HDI) in the printed
circuit board (PCB) are widely applied in 5 G communication, energy
devices, wearable devices, and other booming fields [1–3]. Metallization
of through-hole (TH) is one of the core technologies to realize the con-
duction of different layers in HDI-PCB [4,5]. Acidic sulfate copper
electronic plating is the most universal process for the metallization of
TH [6–9]. TH copper thickening combined with resin plugging and TH
void-free copper filling are the two common metallization technologies.
For the TH copper thickening combined with resin plugging technology,
only a homogeneous and conformal copper coating (about 20 µm) on its
side wall is needed [10–14], then epoxy resin is used to fill the TH. For
the TH void-free copper filling technology, copper coating is fully filled
inside the TH without any void. It is worth noting that TH may crack
under long-term heating due to the different thermal expansion coeffi
cient between the resin and copper, resulting in the blocked signal
transmission. Therefore, compared with TH copper thickening com-
bined with resin plugging technology, TH void-free copper filling tech-
nology behaves the advantages of higher reliability and better signal
transmission quality. Nowadays, with the acceleration of communica-
tion speed, more heat is generated when the signal processing, the
copper void-free filling of TH has therefore been widely employed for
improving the heat dissipation efficiency.
The main difficulty in copper filling is the formation of voids in TH
with higher aspect ratio due to the uneven local current distribution and
tanglesome convection environments caused by the specific geometry of
TH [15–17]. The copper deposition amount at the mouth is usually
higher than that at the center of TH, resulting in the coating in a void or
seam. Therefore, it is particularly crucial introducing the organic addi-
tives in the acidic sulfate bath to modulate the copper deposition process
at the mouth and center. The key to blind hole filling is the bottom-up
growth of copper coating. The key to TH filling is that copper coating
rapidly deposits at the center of TH wall until the center is connected to
form a butterfly shape structure (two blind holes), and then the two
blind holes are filled separately. The accelerator of bis-(3-sulfopropyl)
disulfide (SPS) and suppressor of polyethylene glycol (PEG) are the
commonly used additives in the acidic sulfate bath [18–25]. Suppressor,
mainly distributed at the mouth of TH, inhibits the copper ion
electro-reduction at a definite potential which results in the decrease of
reduction current density. Accelerator, mainly distributed at the center

behaved with the synergistic inhibiting effect with PEG and the antag-

4. Conclusions
It is very important to optimize the novel additive for TH copper
void-free filling. In this work, we first successfully develop a novel SA-
based acidic sulfate copper electronic plating process, and the process
behaves the excellent copper void-free filling of TH. The complicated but
effective molecule actions and synergistic effects among PEG, SPS and
SA are carefully studied for the void-free filling of TH by CV, in situ FTIR
experiments and theoretical calculations. This work is undoubtedly
beneficial to understanding the interaction mechanisms of additives at a
molecular level, and further developing and improving the acidic sulfate
copper electronic plating in TH void-free filling.
